PullRequest.Title: Fix marketplace 403 responses prompting repeated sign-in
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Related to [microsoft/vscode#325412](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325412). Fixes a status regression introduced by [microsoft/vscode#325804](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/325804).

## Changes

Only a service-index `401` requests sign-in. A `403` now follows the existing `AccessDenied` path instead of repeatedly asking an already signed-in user to sign in again. This follows the issue's HTTP/authentication contract and does not infer recoverability from the provider or the presence of a bearer token.

The focused regressions cover default, GitHub, and Microsoft account configurations, anonymous and bearer requests, and both status codes. The existing Entra consent test now verifies recovery from `RequiresSignIn` to `Available` after interactive consent; the sign-out race matrix also covers a late `403`.

No token selection, acquisition, renewal, caching, configuration, UI, or localization changes.

## Validation

Run from the repository root on Windows:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node build\npm\electronTypes.ts` | Passed; restored checksum-verified generated Electron typings. |
| `node node_modules\@typescript\native\bin\tsc --project src\tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck` | Passed. |
| `npm run typecheck-client` | Passed. |
| `npm run transpile-client` | Passed. |
| `$env:VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH = '1'; .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\services\extensionManagement\test\electron-browser\extensionGalleryManifestService.test.ts --reporter dot` | Passed: 74 tests. |
| `npm run valid-layers-check` | Passed. |
| `npm run precommit` | Passed: both changed files. |
| `git diff --cached --check` | Passed. |

The isolated worktree used shared read-only dependencies and an already-prepared Electron runtime; transpiled output is local to this worktree. No live private-marketplace deployment was available for manual testing. Existing status UI, accessible labels, and actions are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup with a configured private marketplace returning HTTP 403
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The eager manifest service resolves the configured account and awaits the service-index request before publishing a null manifest/status and initializing shared-process and optional remote-server channels. The diff does not add an await or boundary; it changes the terminal local status from RequiresSignIn to AccessDenied. `asJson` checks the non-success status and throws before reading or parsing the response body.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve OAuth protected-resource metadata for an eligible Microsoft account when applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one metadata discovery sequence per Microsoft account resolution; zero for the GitHub/default provider path. Effective cardinality is unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider/account resolution and metadata discovery occurred before the changed 403 classification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: For the Microsoft path this completes before the account/token can be returned and before the service-index request proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET the configured marketplace service index.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for the initial coalesced resolution, and one per later account-change resolution; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, the same request was issued and the same 403 response completed; it was classified as MarketplaceAuthRequiredError rather than the generic AccessDenied path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request determines whether a manifest can be published. On 403, response body buffering is skipped by `asJson` because the status is non-success.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the null manifest and cleared authorization to shared-process and optional remote-server channels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per available channel after initial resolution, with later calls only when the manifest value changes. Since both old and new 403 handling publish null, cardinality is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A 403 already resulted in a null manifest and the same channel publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Channel calls are started after manifest resolution and are not awaited by the startup promise.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One coalesced manifest initialization per service instance (`extensionGalleryManifestPromise`), with one configured marketplace service-index URL. Account/provider work is one logical account resolution; no collection fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent `getExtensionGalleryManifest` callers share one promise. Account resolution and the service-index request are awaited serially. Account-change resolutions can overlap but cancel the prior resolution token; that behavior and request cardinality are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The manifest initialization promise coalesces cold callers and remains warm for later callers. Provider session/preferred-account and protected-resource behavior is unchanged. A 403 is not negatively cached separately before or after; it remains the current in-memory status until an account event.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the production hunk only removes 403 from the auth-required branch; traced `asJson` rejects before buffering non-2xx responses, and all network/IPC scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider implementations and network latency vary by deployment, but no boundary count, response buffering, or scheduling changed. The new generic path adds at most the existing error-log calls for a 403, once per resolution, which is not a realistic reportable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The change alters status classification and UI messaging without adding or amplifying expensive work.

Scenarios.Scenario: User views marketplace access state and optionally invokes sign-in after a denied response
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The manifest status event updates context keys and an eventual activity badge. RequiresSignIn previously displayed a sign-in badge/link; AccessDenied displays a warning/contact-administrator message. Authentication begins only if the user explicitly runs the sign-in command, so there is no automatic retry loop on either status.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider sign-in/session creation and possible protected-resource consent when the user invokes the command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero automatically; one provider flow per explicit user command. The changed 403 status removes the normal sign-in affordance for denied users rather than increasing calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A 403 was shown as RequiresSignIn, allowing users to invoke the same sign-in command repeatedly. The PR prevents that UX loop, but the loop was user-driven rather than an automatic performance mechanism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the denied-status rendering path; it runs only after explicit user interaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One local status transition per completed resolution and a constant number of context-key/badge updates. The number of extension rows or installed extensions does not multiply this work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Status consumers run synchronously/event-driven with constant work. Sign-in is user initiated and provider-owned; the diff does not schedule concurrent authentication operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The displayed status is held in memory. No new cache key, invalidation path, positive/negative cache, or retry policy is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all status consumers and the sign-in action were traced, and sign-in is not automatically invoked from the changed status event.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Activity-service rendering cost is not measured, but both statuses create one constant-size badge and one marketplace-access view; no scaling or hot-loop mechanism exists.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The UI work remains constant, and the change reduces the opportunity for repeated user-triggered auth work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Extension gallery manifest service regression tests covering 401/403 providers, bearer states, sign-out races, and consent recovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added cases run only in the test suite. They instantiate mocked services, execute in-memory streams/events, and await deterministic mocked manifest/account flows.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Twelve matrix cases are added for 3 providers x 2 token states x 2 statuses, one extra 403 sign-out-race case, and additional assertions in one consent test. This is fixed test cardinality, not product input scaling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tests execute under the existing test runner; each case awaits its mocked operations. The consent test uses one event promise and disposes its listener through the suite disposable store.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mocks are recreated/reset according to the suite setup; no production cache behavior is changed by test code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: these hunks are confined to the test file and use mocked request/authentication services.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runner scheduling is outside the diff context, but the fixed number of lightweight mocked cases does not establish a product performance regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance finding. The fixed test-runtime increase is expected regression coverage.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. Traced startup/account resolution, HTTP and IPC boundaries, status consumers, sign-in behavior, caching/coalescing, and test-only work. The 403 change does not increase boundary cardinality, concurrency, body buffering, retained state, or critical-path work; no valid performance issue was found.
